issues: No integrity problems found. The candidate adds an atom-pair fingerprint, turns it into 0/1 bits, and averages its Tanimoto kernel with the existing Morgan Tanimoto and descriptor RBF kernels. Test molecules are only featurized from their SMILES. Their labels are never used, and there is no file or network access.
No bugs that make the result meaningless. Train and test kernels are built the same way, and an average of valid kernels is still valid.

Recomputed z = (0.4830 - 0.4843) / (0.0070 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/1)) = -0.0013 / 0.0099 ≈ -0.13. This matches the harness value of -0.128, which differs only through rounding of the displayed losses. Negative z means the candidate is slightly worse, well within noise, so rejecting it is correct.
Minor: every fold now makes an extra atom-pair fingerprint pass and an extra Tanimoto kernel, which adds some runtime for no measured gain.
